:::{#thm-double-exp}

#### Power of a power

If $a > 0$ and $b, c \in \reals$, then

$$a^{bc} = \paren{a^b}^c = \paren{a^c}^b$$
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

:::{#exm-double-exp-negative-base}
#### A negative base

With $a = -1$, $b = 2$, and $c = \frac{1}{2}$:

$$
\ba
a^{bc}
&= (-1)^{2 \cd \frac{1}{2}}
\\
&= (-1)^{1}
\\
&= -1
\ea
$$

but

$$
\ba
\paren{a^b}^c
&= \paren{(-1)^2}^{\frac{1}{2}}
\\
&= 1^{\frac{1}{2}}
\\
&= 1
\ea
$$

So $a^{bc} \neq \paren{a^b}^c$ here,
which is why @thm-double-exp requires $a > 0$.
The third expression, $\paren{a^c}^b = \paren{(-1)^{\frac{1}{2}}}^2$,
is not even a real number.

:::

:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}

:::{.theorem .example}
